nodes.label: Indoor
nodes.description: The shot happens inside a building, so walls, ceilings and lamps decide the light and the space instead of the sky.
examples: a portrait taken inside a room
a figure standing in a lit hallway

nodes.label: Outdoor
nodes.description: The shot happens outside under open sky, so daylight, weather and time of day shape how it looks.
examples: a figure walking under an open sky
a subject photographed in daylight outside

nodes.label: Setting detail
nodes.description: A branch for the smaller features of a place — walls, surfaces, plants, people in the background — that describe a setting without replacing it, so they combine freely with any location.
examples: a plain wall right behind the subject
people moving in the background of a street

nodes.label: Urban
nodes.description: Outdoor places built by people: streets, alleys, rooftops and the structures between them. Pick one of the children when you know which kind of city space you mean.
examples: a subject framed against city buildings

nodes.label: Nature
nodes.description: Outdoor places shaped by landscape rather than buildings — beaches, forests, mountains and open ground.
examples: a figure small against an open landscape

nodes.label: Home interior
nodes.description: Inside somebody’s home. Choose a room below when the exact space matters; on its own it simply says the setting is domestic and lived-in.
examples: a relaxed portrait taken in someone’s flat

nodes.label: Public interior
nodes.description: Indoor spaces open to the public — cafes, bars, shops, galleries, offices and lobbies.
examples: a subject seated in a busy indoor venue

nodes.label: Transit space
nodes.description: Places built for travelling through: stations, terminals, platforms and the inside of vehicles.
examples: a commuter waiting where people pass through

nodes.label: Studio
nodes.description: A controlled shooting space with a built backdrop instead of a real location, so nothing in the background is accidental.
examples: a clean shoot on a built backdrop

nodes.label: Urban street
nodes.description: An ordinary city street with traffic, pavements and shopfronts — the everyday urban backdrop most street photography uses.
examples: a person walking along a city pavement
a figure standing at the kerb of a busy road

nodes.label: Alley
nodes.description: A narrow passage between buildings — tight, shadowed and cluttered, far more enclosed than an ordinary street.
examples: a figure lit by one lamp in a narrow back lane

nodes.label: Rooftop
nodes.description: On top of a building, out in the open with the city spread out below and nothing but sky overhead.
examples: a subject on a roof with the city far beneath them

nodes.label: Bridge
nodes.description: On a structure carrying a road or path over water or rail, where the railings and span make long lines running away from the camera.
examples: a figure halfway across a river bridge

nodes.label: Tunnel
nodes.description: Inside an enclosed passage cut through ground or building, lit only by artificial lights repeating along its length.
examples: a subject walking through a lit underpass

nodes.label: Plaza or square
nodes.description: A wide paved open space in a city where several streets meet, big enough that people and buildings sit far apart.
examples: a lone figure crossing a wide paved square
nodes.negative_fragment: not in an open city square

nodes.label: Parking lot
nodes.description: A flat open area outdoors for parked cars — wide, mostly empty, marked with painted lines and lit by tall lamps after dark.
examples: a subject alone in a wide empty car park at night
nodes.negative_fragment: not in an open-air parking lot

nodes.label: Crosswalk
nodes.description: The striped pedestrian crossing painted across a road. It refines a street rather than replacing it, so it combines with any city street.
examples: a subject stepping onto painted crossing stripes

nodes.label: Night city
nodes.description: A city after dark, where lit windows, street lamps and signs supply nearly all the light. It describes how the place looks, so it sits on top of a specific street, alley or rooftop.
examples: a wet street glowing with shop lights after dark
nodes.prompt_fragment: in a city lit up at night
nodes.negative_fragment: not in a city lit up at night

nodes.label: City skyline
nodes.description: The distant outline of tall buildings seen across the city, usually the backdrop behind the subject rather than the place they stand in.
examples: a rooftop portrait with towers stacked behind

nodes.label: Neon signage
nodes.description: Bright coloured shop and bar signs patterning the walls of a street and throwing coloured light onto everything near them.
examples: a face washed in pink and blue sign light

nodes.label: Storefront
nodes.description: The glazed front of a shop along a street, putting a window, a display and lettering directly behind the subject.
examples: a subject framed by a lit shop window
nodes.prompt_fragment: in front of a shop window
nodes.negative_fragment: not in front of a shop window

nodes.label: Beach
nodes.description: Open sand at the edge of the sea, with water, a far horizon and almost nothing blocking the light.
examples: a figure on wet sand with the sea behind

nodes.label: Forest
nodes.description: Among dense trees, where trunks fill the background and light reaches the subject only in broken patches.
examples: a subject standing between tall trunks in dappled light

nodes.label: Mountain
nodes.description: High ground of slopes and rock with very long views, so the horizon sits far away and often far below the subject.
examples: a small figure on a ridge above a valley

nodes.label: Desert
nodes.description: Dry open land of sand or bare earth with almost nothing in it, so the subject stands alone against a huge empty background.
examples: a lone figure on a dune under hard sun

nodes.label: Open field
nodes.description: Flat open ground covered in grass or crops, with a low horizon and a very large area of sky above the subject.
examples: a subject waist-deep in long grass under wide sky

nodes.label: Riverside
nodes.description: Beside moving water — a river, canal or lake edge — where the surface mirrors the sky and bounces light back onto the subject.
examples: a figure on a canal path with water reflecting the sky

nodes.label: Park
nodes.description: A planted public green space inside a town, with grass, paths and trees but city buildings never far away.
examples: a bench portrait under park trees

nodes.label: Bedroom
nodes.description: A private room built around a bed, usually soft and quiet and lit by one window or a single bedside lamp.
examples: morning light across an unmade bed

nodes.label: Living room
nodes.description: The main shared room of a home, with seating, a low table and everyday clutter arranged around the subject.
examples: a subject curled on a sofa in lamplight

nodes.label: Kitchen
nodes.description: The room where food is prepared, full of counters, cupboards and hard reflective surfaces that bounce light around.
examples: a subject leaning on a kitchen counter

nodes.label: Bathroom
nodes.description: A small tiled room with a mirror, a basin and hard surfaces, where light bounces and reflections become part of the picture.
examples: a mirror portrait over a small tiled basin

nodes.label: Cafe
nodes.description: A small place serving coffee, with tables, a counter and big windows — one of the most common everyday interiors for portraits.
examples: a subject by a cafe window with a cup on the table

nodes.label: Restaurant
nodes.description: An indoor dining room with laid tables and warm low lighting hung over each seat.
examples: a couple at a candlelit dinner table

nodes.label: Bar
nodes.description: A dark drinking room lit by small warm lamps and the bottles behind the counter, with deep shadow between each light.
examples: a figure at a bar counter under one hanging lamp

nodes.label: Gallery or museum
nodes.description: A quiet exhibition room with plain walls, even light and a lot of empty space around the subject.
examples: a viewer dwarfed by a white gallery wall

nodes.label: Library
nodes.description: A room lined with bookshelves and reading tables, usually calm and evenly lit from above.
examples: a reader between tall shelves of books

nodes.label: Hotel lobby
nodes.description: The large public entrance hall of a hotel, with seating groups, polished floors and a mix of lamp and daylight.
examples: a traveller waiting in a polished lobby

nodes.label: Convenience store
nodes.description: A small brightly lit shop of packed shelves under hard overhead strip lighting — flat, colourful and unmistakably late-night.
examples: a subject at a bright shop fridge after midnight

nodes.label: Office
nodes.description: A place of work with desks, screens and ceiling lights, often glass-walled and evenly bright everywhere.
examples: a subject at a desk beside a glass partition

nodes.label: Parking garage
nodes.description: A concrete structure of parking floors with low ceilings, pillars and rows of harsh overhead lights — a favourite gritty urban interior.
examples: a figure between concrete pillars under strip lights
nodes.negative_fragment: not in a concrete parking garage

nodes.label: Subway station
nodes.description: A rail station platform above or below ground, with tiled walls, signage and trains arriving beside the subject.
examples: a subject alone on a tiled platform as a train blurs past

nodes.label: Subway train interior
nodes.description: Inside a moving carriage, with handrails, bench seats, darkening windows and evenly spaced ceiling lights.
examples: a commuter holding a rail in a lit carriage

nodes.label: Airport terminal
nodes.description: The large glass-walled hall of an airport, with wide floors, gates, signage and daylight pouring through full-height windows.
examples: a traveller crossing a wide bright departure hall

nodes.label: Car interior
nodes.description: Inside a car, framed by the seat, the window and the windscreen, with light entering from outside and shifting as the car moves.
examples: a passenger lit by passing street lamps

nodes.label: Seamless studio backdrop
nodes.description: A plain roll of coloured paper behind the subject with no visible corner or floor line, so nothing in the background competes with them.
examples: a clean portrait on plain grey paper
nodes.negative_fragment: not against a seamless studio backdrop

nodes.label: Cyclorama studio
nodes.description: A built studio wall that curves smoothly into the floor, so the space around the subject looks endless in every direction.
examples: a full-length figure in an endless white space
nodes.negative_fragment: not in a white cyclorama studio

nodes.label: Green screen
nodes.description: A flat green wall used so the background can be replaced later; the background itself carries no scene information at all.
examples: a subject standing in front of a flat green wall
nodes.prompt_fragment: in front of a green screen
nodes.negative_fragment: not in front of a green screen

nodes.label: Crowded setting
nodes.description: Other people fill the space around the subject, so the frame feels busy and the subject has to be picked out of a moving mass.
examples: a face held still inside a blurred moving crowd
nodes.prompt_fragment: surrounded by a crowd of people
nodes.negative_fragment: not surrounded by a crowd of people

nodes.label: Empty space
nodes.description: The place is empty of other people, which isolates the subject and gives the setting a still, quiet feeling.
examples: a single figure on a deserted street at dawn
nodes.negative_fragment: not in an empty, deserted space

nodes.label: Graffiti wall
nodes.description: A wall covered in spray-painted art or tags, putting a loud colourful pattern directly behind the subject.
examples: a portrait against a painted wall of tags

nodes.label: Brick wall
nodes.description: A plain brick surface right behind the subject — a simple textured backdrop that keeps the background flat and close.
examples: a subject leaning back on old red brick

nodes.label: Greenery
nodes.description: Plants and leaves in the frame, indoors or out, adding green shapes and soft shadow patterns around the subject.
examples: leaves crossing the front of the frame

nodes.label: Staircase
nodes.description: Steps in the frame, indoors or outdoors, which add strong diagonal lines and let the subject sit above or below the camera.
examples: a figure seated halfway up a concrete stairwell

nodes.label: Window view
nodes.description: A window is part of the setting, letting outside light in and showing a slice of whatever lies beyond the room.
examples: a subject sitting against bright window glass

nodes.label: Daytime
nodes.description: Any time between sunrise and sunset, when the sun itself is the main light in the picture.
examples: a scene lit by plain daylight

nodes.label: Morning
nodes.description: The first hours after sunrise, when the sun is still low and the light is soft, clean and slanted across everything.
examples: low clean light across an empty street

nodes.label: Midday
nodes.description: The middle of the day with the sun almost straight overhead, which gives short hard shadows and very bright, contrasty light.
examples: hard short shadows directly under the subject

nodes.label: Afternoon
nodes.description: The stretch after noon when the sun starts dropping again and shadows grow longer and warmer.
examples: long warm shadows stretching down a pavement

nodes.label: Golden hour
nodes.description: The hour just after sunrise or just before sunset, when sunlight travels low through the air and turns warm, golden and soft on skin.
examples: warm low sun grazing across a face

nodes.label: Twilight
nodes.description: The in-between period when the sun is under the horizon but the sky is still lit, so there is light in the scene without a visible sun.
examples: a sky still glowing after the sun has gone

nodes.label: Dawn
nodes.description: The first light in the sky before the sun itself appears — cool, dim, and usually very quiet and empty.
examples: a cold pale sky over an empty road

nodes.label: Sunrise
nodes.description: The moment the sun clears the horizon and throws long low light straight across the scene.
examples: a long shadow thrown by the first sun

nodes.label: Sunset
nodes.description: The moment the sun drops below the horizon, with the strongest colour of the day left behind in the sky.
examples: an orange sky behind a silhouetted figure

nodes.label: Blue hour
nodes.description: The short window after sunset (or before sunrise) when the sky goes deep blue and street lights are already on but the sky is not black yet.
examples: a deep blue sky above warm shop lights

nodes.label: Dusk
nodes.description: The end of twilight as the last light drains out of the sky and artificial lights take over the scene.
examples: street lamps coming on against a fading sky

nodes.label: Night
nodes.description: After dark, when the sun is gone and every light in the picture is artificial, from the moon, or from the city itself.
examples: a subject lit only by shop windows and street lamps

nodes.label: Evening
nodes.description: The early part of the night, when it is fully dark outside but streets, homes and shops are still busy and lit.
examples: warm windows along a dark street still full of people

nodes.label: Midnight
nodes.description: The deepest part of the night, when almost nothing is still lit and the streets are empty.
examples: a single lit sign on an otherwise black street
nodes.negative_fragment: not in the dead of night

nodes.label: Clear sky
nodes.description: An open sky with no cloud in the way, so sunlight lands directly on the scene and every shadow has a hard edge.
examples: hard sun and a deep blue sky

nodes.label: Cloudy
nodes.description: Cloud is present in the sky, softening the sunlight without shutting it out completely.
examples: soft sun coming and going behind cloud

nodes.label: Partly cloudy
nodes.description: Separate clouds drift across an otherwise open sky, so the light keeps switching between hard sun and soft shade.
examples: bright sun between drifting clouds

nodes.label: Overcast
nodes.description: The sky is completely covered by cloud, which turns it into one huge soft light source: shadows nearly vanish and colours go flat and cool.
examples: even shadowless light under a white sky
nodes.negative_fragment: not under a flat overcast sky

nodes.label: Rain
nodes.description: Water is falling from the sky, which darkens the scene, puts streaks in the air and makes every surface wet and reflective.
examples: rain streaks crossing a lit street

nodes.label: Drizzle
nodes.description: Very fine rain that barely shows in the air but still soaks surfaces and dulls the light.
examples: a faint wet sheen with no visible drops

nodes.label: Heavy rain
nodes.description: Rain hard enough to be a visible wall of water, bouncing off the ground and hiding whatever is far away.
examples: rain bouncing off the road around a figure

nodes.label: Snow
nodes.description: Snow is falling, filling the air with slow white flakes and muffling both contrast and colour.
examples: flakes drifting through lamp light

nodes.label: Blizzard
nodes.description: Snow driven hard by wind until the air is nearly white and anything more than a few steps away disappears.
examples: a figure half lost in driving white snow

nodes.label: Thunderstorm
nodes.description: A storm of dark towering cloud, lightning and rain, where the light can jump from very dark to blindingly bright in an instant.
examples: a black sky split by a lightning flash

nodes.label: Atmospherics
nodes.description: Secondary conditions in the air or on the ground. They sit on top of whatever the main weather is, so combinations like rain plus fog are normal rather than contradictory.
examples: thin air and a wet road under one sky
nodes.prompt_fragment: with visible atmosphere in the air
nodes.negative_fragment: no visible atmosphere in the air

nodes.label: Fog
nodes.description: Thick water vapour in the air that hides everything past a short distance and turns anything further away into a soft grey outline.
examples: street lamps as soft glowing balls in grey air
nodes.prompt_fragment: with thick fog in the air
nodes.negative_fragment: no thick fog in the air

nodes.label: Mist
nodes.description: A light version of fog: you can still see across the scene, but the air is visibly soft and distance goes pale.
examples: pale soft air over an early field
nodes.prompt_fragment: with light mist hanging in the air
nodes.negative_fragment: no light mist hanging in the air

nodes.label: Haze
nodes.description: A thin veil of heat, dust or pollution that lowers contrast and fades whatever is far away into the sky.
examples: a skyline fading into milky white air
nodes.prompt_fragment: with a hazy veil in the air
nodes.negative_fragment: no hazy veil in the air

nodes.label: Wind
nodes.description: Moving air you can actually see in the picture — hair, clothing, trees and dust all pushed the same way.
examples: hair and coat pulled sideways by a gust
nodes.prompt_fragment: with wind moving through the scene
nodes.negative_fragment: no wind moving through the scene

nodes.label: Wet ground
nodes.description: The ground is still wet after rain, so pavements and roads mirror lights and sky back up even once the rain has stopped.
examples: neon reflected in a puddle on black asphalt

nodes.label: Snow on the ground
nodes.description: Snow already lying on surfaces, bouncing light back up under the subject, whether or not it is still snowing.
examples: bright bounce light off a white street
nodes.prompt_fragment: with snow lying on the ground
nodes.negative_fragment: no snow lying on the ground

nodes.label: Carried items
nodes.description: Things the subject carries with them, usually bags and luggage, which change how they stand and where their hands end up.
examples: a bag pulling one shoulder down

nodes.label: Handheld objects
nodes.description: Small objects held in the hands, which give the subject something to do and anchor an otherwise empty pose.
examples: both hands busy with a small object

nodes.label: Vehicles
nodes.description: A vehicle in the frame that the subject rides, leans on, pushes or simply stands beside.
examples: a subject resting against something they ride

nodes.label: Furniture
nodes.description: Pieces of furniture used in the shot, which decide whether the subject sits, leans, perches or rests on something.
examples: a piece of furniture holding the pose up

nodes.label: Suitcase
nodes.description: A rigid travel case, usually on wheels, that instantly reads as travelling and gives the subject something to pull or lean on.
examples: a traveller with a wheeled case beside them

nodes.label: Shopping bag
nodes.description: A paper or plastic bag from a shop, hanging from one hand and swinging as the subject walks.
examples: a paper bag swinging at one side

nodes.label: Briefcase
nodes.description: A flat rigid case for documents, held in one hand — formal, and it locks that arm straight down.
examples: one arm held stiff by a flat case

nodes.label: Coffee cup
nodes.description: A cup of coffee in the hand — the most common everyday hand prop, and an easy excuse for a relaxed natural gesture.
examples: a paper cup held at chest height

nodes.label: Umbrella
nodes.description: An umbrella held overhead, which shelters the subject, frames their head and drops its own shadow across them.
examples: a dark canopy held above a lit face

nodes.label: Camera
nodes.description: A camera in the subject’s hands, which tells the viewer they are the one taking pictures.
examples: a camera raised toward the viewer

nodes.label: Smartphone
nodes.description: A phone in the hand, which pulls the head down and lights the face from below when the screen is on.
examples: a face lit from below by a screen

nodes.label: Book
nodes.description: A book held open or closed in the hands, which lowers the gaze and makes the subject look occupied and still.
examples: an open paperback held in both hands

nodes.label: Cigarette
nodes.description: A lit cigarette, which adds a small point of light, a rising line of smoke and a very specific mood.
examples: a thin line of smoke crossing a dark frame

nodes.label: Flower bouquet
nodes.description: A bunch of cut flowers held in the arms or hands, adding a bright block of colour right under the face.
examples: a wrapped bunch of flowers held to the chest
nodes.negative_fragment: not holding a bouquet of flowers

nodes.label: Bicycle
nodes.description: A bicycle ridden, pushed or leaned on, which spreads the subject’s stance and puts strong thin lines through the frame.
examples: a rider standing over a bike at a kerb

nodes.label: Motorcycle
nodes.description: A motorbike or scooter in the frame, heavier and lower than a bicycle and usually the loudest shape in the picture.
examples: a rider seated on a parked motorbike

nodes.label: Car
nodes.description: A car in the frame — parked, leaned on or being got into — which supplies both a large surface and reflections.
examples: a figure leaning on a car door

nodes.label: Skateboard
nodes.description: A skateboard underfoot, carried under an arm or tipped up on its tail, which reads immediately as street culture.
examples: a board held upright beside the leg

nodes.label: Chair
nodes.description: A chair in the shot, which fixes where the subject sits and how their arms and legs can fall.
examples: a subject turned sideways on a wooden chair

nodes.label: Stool
nodes.description: A backless seat, often high, which keeps the whole body visible and lets the legs hang or brace.
examples: a perched figure with one foot on a rung

nodes.label: Bench
nodes.description: A long shared seat, usually outdoors, that lets the subject sit, sprawl or lie along a strong horizontal line.
examples: a figure lying along a park bench

nodes.label: Table
nodes.description: A table or desk in front of the subject, which gives the arms somewhere to rest and cuts the body at a clean line.
examples: elbows resting on a small cafe table

nodes.label: Ladder
nodes.description: A ladder leaned or standing in the frame, which lets the subject climb, perch or sit high and adds a strong repeating line.
examples: a subject seated on the top step of a ladder
